instrument.title: Road Safety Road Rules 2017 (Vic)
instrument.citation: S.R. No. 41/2017, Version No. 027 incorporating amendments as at 27 October 2026 — Part 12 Restrictions on stopping and parking; rules 316–318; Schedule 1

rules.title: No stopping signs
rules.plain: You must not stop at all, for any reason, while a NO STOPPING (or older NO STANDING) sign applies. Not even to drop someone off.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a length of road or in an area to which a no stopping sign applies. 3 penalty units.

rules.title: No parking signs
rules.plain: While a NO PARKING sign applies you may stop only to drop off or pick up passengers or goods, must not leave the vehicle unattended (more than 3 m away), and must drive on within 2 minutes (or the time shown on the sign; 5 minutes with an accessible parking permit).
rules.quote: (1) The driver of a vehicle must not stop on a length of road or in an area to which a no parking sign applies, unless the driver— (a) is dropping off, or picking up, passengers or goods; and (b) does not leave the vehicle unattended; and (c) completes the dropping off, or picking up ... within the required time after stopping. (2) ... a driver leaves a vehicle unattended if the driver leaves the vehicle so the driver is over 3 metres from the closest point of the vehicle. (3) required time means— (a) if information on or with the sign indicates a time—the indicated time; or (b) if there is no indicated time—2 minutes; or (c) ... rule 206 applies to the driver—5 minutes.

rules.title: No stopping on a road with a yellow edge line
rules.plain: A continuous yellow line along the edge of the road means NO STOPPING, whether or not there is a sign.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop at the side of a road marked with a continuous yellow edge line.

rules.title: Stopping near an intersection with traffic lights
rules.plain: Don't stop within 20 m of an intersection with traffic lights unless you are at a place covered by a parking control sign that permits it.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a road within 20 metres from the nearest point of an intersecting road at an intersection with traffic lights, unless the driver stops at a place on a length of road, or in an area, to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping near an intersection without traffic lights
rules.plain: Don't stop within 10 m of an intersection without traffic lights, unless a parking sign permits it or you're on the continuous side of a T-intersection.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a road within 10 metres from the nearest point of an intersecting road at an intersection without traffic lights, unless the driver stops— (a) at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop ...; or (b) if the intersection is a T-intersection—along the continuous side of the continuing road at the intersection.

rules.title: Stopping on or near a children's crossing
rules.plain: Don't stop on a children's crossing, or within 20 m before and 10 m after it, unless a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a children's crossing, or on the road within 20 metres before the crossing and 10 metres after the crossing unless the driver stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping on or near a pedestrian crossing (except at an intersection)
rules.plain: Don't stop on a pedestrian (zebra) crossing, or within 20 m before and 10 m after it, unless a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a pedestrian crossing that is not at an intersection, or on the road within 20 metres before the crossing and 10 metres after the crossing, unless the driver stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping on or near a marked foot crossing (except at an intersection)
rules.plain: At a signalised pedestrian crossing: don't stop within 10 m before the nearest traffic-lights pole and 3 m after the crossing.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a marked foot crossing that is not at an intersection, or on the road within 10 metres before the traffic lights pole nearest to the driver at the crossing and 3 metres after the crossing, unless ... a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop ...

rules.title: Stopping on a clearway
rules.plain: You must not stop on a clearway while the CLEARWAY sign applies (buses and commercial passenger vehicles may stop to pick up/drop off). Vehicles are commonly towed. The clearway runs from the sign to the next clearway sign with different times, an END CLEARWAY sign, or the end of the road.
rules.quote: (1) A driver must not stop on a length of road to which a clearway sign applies, unless subrule (2) or (3) applies to the driver. 3 penalty units. ... (4) A clearway sign applies, for the days or times indicated on the sign, to the length of road beginning at the sign and ending at the nearer of the following— (a) a clearway sign on the road that indicates different days or times; (b) an end clearway sign on the road; (c) the end of the road.

rules.title: Stopping in a loading zone
rules.plain: Only buses and commercial passenger vehicles (dropping off/picking up passengers), trucks, signed courier/delivery vehicles, taxis, and vehicles built mainly for carrying loads (not sedans, station wagons or motorbikes) that are loading or unloading goods may stop in a LOADING ZONE. Max 30 minutes unless the sign shows another time. Ordinary cars must not stop, even to load.
rules.quote: (1) A driver must not stop in a loading zone unless the driver is driving— (a) a bus that is dropping off, or picking up, passengers; or (ab) a commercial passenger vehicle ... (c) a truck that is dropping off, or picking up, goods; or (d) a courier vehicle displaying a courier vehicle sign ...; or (e) a delivery vehicle displaying a delivery vehicle sign ...; or (f) a vehicle (other than a sedan, station wagon or motor bike) that is dropping off, or picking up, goods which is constructed principally for carrying loads ...; or (g) a taxi that is dropping off, or picking up, passengers or goods. (2) A driver who is permitted to stop in a loading zone must not stay continuously in the zone for longer than— (a) 30 minutes; or (b) if information on or with the loading zone sign ... indicates another time—the indicated time.

rules.title: Stopping in a truck zone
rules.plain: Only a truck (over 4.5 t) dropping off or picking up goods may stop in a TRUCK ZONE.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a truck zone unless the driver is driving a truck that is dropping off, or picking up, goods.

sources.note: r 180; 'truck' defined in dictionary (over 4.5 t GVM)

rules.title: Stopping in a works zone
rules.plain: Only vehicles engaged in construction work in or near the zone may stop in a WORKS ZONE.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a works zone unless the driver is driving a vehicle that is engaged in construction work in or near the zone.

rules.title: Stopping in a taxi zone
rules.plain: Only taxis may stop in a TAXI ZONE.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a taxi zone, unless the driver is driving a taxi.

rules.title: Stopping in a bus zone
rules.plain: Only public buses may stop in a BUS ZONE (unless the sign excludes a kind of bus).
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a bus zone unless the driver is driving a public bus (except a public bus of a kind that is not permitted to stop in the bus zone by information on or with the bus zone sign ...).

rules.title: Stopping in a minibus zone
rules.plain: Only public minibuses may stop in a MINIBUS ZONE.
rules.quote: A driver (except the driver of a public minibus) must not stop in a minibus zone.

rules.title: Stopping in a permit zone
rules.plain: You must not stop in a PERMIT ZONE unless your vehicle displays (or you hold electronically) a current permit issued by the council for that zone, e.g. 'Area 1A' resident permit.
rules.quote: (1) Subject to subrule (3), a driver must not stop in a permit zone unless the driver's vehicle displays a current permit issued by the person or body responsible for the care and management of the permit zone that permits the vehicle to stop in the zone. ... (3) A driver may stop in a permit zone without displaying a current permit ... if the permit is otherwise held by the driver in a manner determined to be appropriate by the person or body responsible ...

rules.title: Stopping in a mail zone
rules.plain: Nobody may stop in a MAIL ZONE except exempted postal vehicles.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a mail zone.

rules.title: Double parking
rules.plain: Don't stop between a parked vehicle and the centre of the road.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a road if to do so would put any part of the vehicle that the driver is driving between a vehicle that is parked on the road and the centre of the road.

rules.title: Stopping in or near a safety zone
rules.plain: Don't stop in a safety zone (tram stop island) or within 10 m before or after it, unless a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop in a safety zone, or on a road within 10 metres before or after a safety zone, unless the driver stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping near a fire hydrant etc.
rules.plain: Don't stop within 1 m of a fire hydrant, fire hydrant indicator or fire plug indicator.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop within 1 metre of a fire hydrant, fire hydrant indicator, or fire plug indicator, unless— (a) the driver is driving a public bus ... (b) ... a taxi ... (c) ... a public minibus ...

rules.title: Stopping at or near a bus stop
rules.plain: Don't stop within 20 m before or 10 m after a bus stop sign, unless a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver (except the driver of a public bus) must not stop at a bus stop, or on the road, within 20 metres before a sign on the road that indicates the bus stop, and within 10 metres after the sign, unless the driver stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping at or near a tram stop
rules.plain: Don't stop at a tram stop or within 20 m before the tram stop sign, unless a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver (except the driver of a tram, a tram recovery vehicle or a public bus travelling along tram tracks) must not stop at a tram stop or on the road within 20 metres before a sign on the road that indicates the tram stop, unless— (a) the driver stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies; and (b) the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping on a path, dividing strip, nature strip, painted island or traffic island
rules.plain: Don't stop on a footpath, shared path, dividing strip, nature strip (in a built-up area), painted island or traffic island — not even partly. Motorcycles may stop on a path if they don't obstruct anyone.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a bicycle path, footpath, shared path or dividing strip, or a nature strip adjacent to a length of road in a built-up area, unless— (a) ... a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop ...; or (b) the driver's vehicle is a motor cycle and the driver stops in a place where the motor cycle does not inconvenience, obstruct, hinder or prevent the free passage of any pedestrian or other vehicle ...

rules.title: Obstructing access to and from a footpath, driveway etc.
rules.plain: Don't stop on or across a driveway (including your own) — you may park up to its edge. Exception: dropping off/picking up passengers, staying with the car, and driving on within 2 minutes.
rules.quote: (2) A driver must not stop on or across a driveway or other way of access for vehicles travelling to or from adjacent land unless— (a) the driver— (i) is dropping off, or picking up, passengers; and (ii) does not leave the vehicle unattended; and (iii) completes the dropping off, or picking up, of the passengers, and drives on, as soon as possible and, in any case, within 2 minutes after stopping; or (b) the driver stops in a parking bay and the driver is permitted to stop in the parking bay under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping near a postbox
rules.plain: Don't stop within 3 m of a public postbox unless dropping off/picking up passengers or mail, or a parking sign permits it.
rules.quote: A driver must not stop on a road within 3 metres of a public postbox, unless the driver— (a) is dropping off, or picking up, passengers or mail; or (b) stops at a place ... to which a parking control sign applies and the driver is permitted to stop at that place under these Rules.

rules.title: Stopping on a road with a bicycle parking sign
rules.plain: Only bicycles (and e-scooters) may stop where a BICYCLE PARKING sign applies, except to drop off or pick up passengers.
rules.quote: A driver (except the rider of a bicycle or an electric scooter) must not stop on a length of road to which a bicycle parking sign applies, unless the driver is dropping off, or picking up, passengers.

rules.title: Stopping on a road with a motor bike parking sign
rules.plain: Only motorbikes may stop where a MOTOR BIKE PARKING / MOTOR BIKES ONLY sign applies, except to drop off or pick up passengers.
rules.quote: A driver (except the rider of a motor bike) must not stop on a length of road to which a motor bike parking sign applies, unless the driver is dropping off, or picking up, passengers.

sources.note: City of Melbourne footpath motorcycle parking

rules.title: Stopping in an accessible parking area
rules.plain: You must not stop in an accessible (disabled) parking bay unless your vehicle displays a current accessible parking permit and you follow its conditions.
rules.quote: (1) A driver must not stop in an accessible parking area unless— (a) the driver's vehicle displays a current accessible parking permit; and (b) the driver complies with the conditions of use of the permit. Penalty: 2 penalty units. ... (6) An accessible parking area is a length or area of a road (including a parking bay)— (a) to which a permissive parking sign displaying an accessibility symbol applies; or (b) to which an accessible parking sign applies; or (c) indicated by a road marking ... that consists of, or includes, an accessibility symbol.

sources.note: r 203 as substituted by S.R. No. 182/2026

rules.title: Time extension for people with an accessible parking permit
rules.plain: If your vehicle displays a current accessible parking permit, you may park for twice the time shown on an ordinary (green P) sign. The doubling does not apply inside an accessible parking bay itself.
rules.quote: (1) This rule applies to a driver if— (a) the driver's vehicle displays a current accessible parking permit; and (b) the driver complies with the conditions of use of the permit. (2) The driver may park continuously on a length of road, or in an area, to which a permissive parking sign applies (except in an accessible parking area) for twice the period indicated on the sign.

sources.note: r 206 as substituted by S.R. No. 182/2026

verification.notes: Fee exemptions for permit holders vary by council and are not modelled.

rules.title: Stopping in a parking area for electric-powered vehicles / for charging
rules.plain: Only electric vehicles may stop in an EV bay; in an EV CHARGING bay the vehicle must also be plugged in.
rules.quote: 203B(1) A driver of a vehicle that is not an electric-powered vehicle must not stop in a parking area for electric-powered vehicles. ... 203C(1) A driver must not stop in a parking area for the charging of electric-powered vehicles unless— (a) the driver's vehicle is an electric-powered vehicle; and (b) the electric-powered vehicle is plugged in to an external source of electricity.

rules.title: Meaning of certain information on or with permissive parking signs
rules.plain: A number (or fraction) to the left of P is the maximum time in hours: 2P = 2 hours, 1/2P = 30 min, 1/4P = 15 min. A number with 'minute' to the right of P is minutes. Times and days on the sign limit when it applies; no days shown = every day.
rules.quote: (2) A whole number, fraction, or whole number and fraction, immediately to the left of the letter "P" indicates that a driver must not park on the length of road, or in the area, continuously for longer than the period of hours, or fraction of an hour, equal to the number, fraction, or number and fraction, shown. (3) A number, together with the word "minute", immediately to the right of the letter "P" indicate that a driver must not park ... continuously for longer than the number of minutes shown.

rules.title: Parking for longer than indicated
rules.plain: You must not park longer than the time shown on the sign (or double that with an accessible parking permit). The clock runs from when you park until the vehicle is moved off that length of road or out of the area. A plain P sign with no time and no hours means you may park at any time, for any length, unless another sign prohibits it.
rules.quote: (1) A driver must not park continuously on a length of road, or in an area, to which a permissive parking sign applies for longer than the period indicated by information on or with the sign or, if rule 206 applies to the driver, the period allowed under that rule. 2 penalty units. (1A) If a permissive parking sign does not indicate a period and does not indicate that it applies at particular times ... a driver may, at any time, park continuously ... unless— (a) another parking control sign applies ...; and (b) the driver is prohibited from parking ... under these Rules. (2) ... a driver parks continuously ... from the time when the driver parks on the length of road, or in the area, until the driver, or another driver, moves the vehicle off the length of road, or out of the area ...

rules.title: Parking outside times indicated
rules.plain: When a time-limited sign shows hours/days, you may park there outside those hours/days with no limit from that sign, unless another sign prohibits parking at that time. The engine uses this: a limit stops applying when the sign's window ends.
rules.quote: If a permissive parking sign indicates that it applies at particular times, or at particular times on particular days, a driver may park on the length of road, or in an area, to which the sign applies at a time, or at a time on a day, when the sign does not apply, unless— (a) another parking control sign applies to the length of road or area; and (b) the driver is prohibited from parking on the length of road, or in the area, at that time, or at that time on that day, under these Rules.

verification.notes: Open question for contributors: whether a stay that begins inside the window and runs past its end is measured only against the window (practice: yes, the limit ceases at window end). Engine assumes yes.

rules.title: Parking where fees are payable
rules.plain: Where the sign shows a fee is payable (TICKET / METER / PAY), you must pay the fee and obey any instructions on or with the sign, as well as the time limit.
rules.quote: (1) This rule applies to a driver who parks on a length of road, or in an area, to which a permissive parking sign applies if information on or with the sign indicates that a fee is payable for parking. (2) The driver must— (a) pay the fee (if any); and (b) obey any instructions on or with the sign. 2 penalty units.

rules.title: Parallel parking on a road (except in a median strip parking area)
rules.plain: Park facing the direction of travel, parallel and as close as practicable to the kerb; at least 1 m from vehicles in front and behind; at least 3 m from a continuous dividing line or dividing strip (or leave 3 m clear alongside if there is no line); don't unreasonably obstruct others.
rules.quote: (5) If the driver does not park in a parking bay, the driver must position the vehicle at least 1 metre from the closest point of any vehicle in front of it and any vehicle behind it. (6) If the road has a continuous dividing line or a dividing strip, the driver must position the vehicle at least 3 metres from the continuous dividing line or dividing strip ... (7) If the road does not have a continuous dividing line or a dividing strip, the driver must position the vehicle so there is at least 3 metres of the road alongside the vehicle that is clear for other vehicles to pass ...

rules.title: Signs may be arranged differently and still apply
rules.plain: A parking sign still counts even if its layout, arrow direction, number of panels or extra information differs from the standard diagram, or it is combined with other signs on one panel.
rules.quote: A traffic sign may be a reasonable likeness of a diagram ... even though— ... (d) the sign has a different number of panels; or (e) the sign is combined on a single panel with one or more other traffic signs; or (f) for a parking control sign—words, figures, symbols, or anything else, on the sign are differently arranged; or (g) for a ... parking control sign—the sign has an arrow pointing in a different direction ...

rules.title: Limited effect of certain traffic control devices (times, days, public holidays)
rules.plain: A sign that shows times/days applies only at those times/days. A sign that names a day of the week does NOT apply on a public holiday unless the sign says otherwise. A sign with no days shown applies every day, including public holidays.
rules.quote: (1) If information on a traffic control device indicates that the device applies during particular times, on particular days ... the device has effect only for the indicated times, days ... (3) If information on a traffic control device that is at a place indicates that it applies on a particular day of the week, the device does not have effect on a day that is a public holiday for the place unless information on the device states otherwise. Example: If a loading zone sign indicates that it applies on Monday to Friday between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. and information on or with the sign does not indicate that it applies on public holidays, the sign does not have effect on any public holiday falling on a Monday to Friday.

sources.note: Melbourne applies this to the holiday AND any declared day in lieu
Yarra: holiday only, not day in lieu

verification.notes: 'Public holiday' = appointed under the Public Holidays Act 1993 (Vic). Day-in-lieu treatment differs between councils.
